universities.name: University of Mostar Faculty of Medicine
universities.summary: University of Mostar Faculty of Medicine is a public medical school in Mostar, Bosnia and Herzegovina. Its full-time Medical Studies in English programme is a direct-entry, six-year, 360-ECTS Doctor of Medicine degree. The school is listed in the World Directory of Medical Schools and the University of Mostar is recorded in Bosnia and Herzegovina's state register of accredited higher-education institutions through February 2028.
universities.campusLifestyle: The English programme is delivered by the University of Mostar School of Medicine in Mostar. Its published curriculum covers 12 semesters and 360 ECTS, and includes basic and clinical medical courses, public health, student organisations and academic work. The faculty's curriculum describes attendance as obligatory and says traditional in-person teaching is preferred, with online teaching capped at 20% at programme level.
universities.cityProfile: Mostar is the programme location. The School of Medicine's official contact address for Medical Studies in English is Kralja Petra Krešimira IV bb, 88000 Mostar. This package does not use unsourced claims about local rent, food, transport or safety; those costs need a separate current student-living source before they are presented as a budget.
universities.practicalExposure: The curriculum places clinical rotations in the sixth and final year. It specifies 12 weeks of student practice across Internal Medicine, Surgery, Gynaecology and Paediatrics, with three weeks in each rotation. The programme also describes clinical rotations as professional practice and says the final year integrates previously acquired knowledge and skills. The English admission call confirms that the degree title is Doctor of Medicine and notes professional work in Bosnia and Herzegovina is subject to the published state-exam condition for independent work.
universities.hostelOverview: No Medicine-specific accommodation provider, bed allocation or current residence price was verified in the official materials used for this package. Accommodation is therefore not included in the fee total and no hostel claim is displayed as a programme benefit.
universities.dietarySupport: No official Medicine-specific meal-plan or dietary-support arrangement was identified in the current admission call or published curriculum. Food and day-to-day spending need to be budgeted separately from tuition and the admission fee.
universities.safetyOverview: The reviewed official programme materials do not publish campus-safety statistics or an emergency-support service for Medical Studies in English. The application route provides direct contacts for the English medical-studies office and the Student Service Office.
universities.studentSupport: The 2026/27 admission call lists an Office for Medical Studies in English and a Student Service Office with named contacts and telephone numbers. It also explains receipt confirmation for submitted documents and requires applicants to reconfirm the confirmation email, creating a documented application-support route rather than a generic support claim.

A current 2026/27 English-programme call with 30 full-time places for Bosnia and Herzegovina citizens or foreign citizens.

faq.question: Is Medical Studies in English at the University of Mostar direct-entry after secondary school?
faq.answer: Yes. The 2026/27 call requires completed secondary education or its equivalent and uses the overall four-year school average, with specific consideration of Biology, Chemistry and Physics grades, as priority selection criteria.

faq.question: How long is the Medical Studies in English degree?
faq.answer: The published curriculum describes an integrated university programme lasting six years across 12 semesters, carrying 360 ECTS credits and leading to the Doctor of Medicine title.

faq.question: What is the annual tuition for 2026/27?
faq.answer: The School of Medicine's 2026/27 English-programme call states annual tuition of 18,000 BAM, plus a 140 BAM admission fee. Tuition is due within one week of the formal electronic acceptance letter and the call states that tuition fees are non-refundable.

faq.question: How many English Medicine places are available in 2026/27?
faq.answer: The first 2026/27 call states that 30 full-time places are planned for Bosnia and Herzegovina citizens or foreign citizens. The published deadline is 30 September 2026 or earlier if all places are filled.

faq.question: What documents does an international applicant need?
faq.answer: The call lists a passport copy, birth certificate in English, diploma and certified copies with official Croatian translation, foreign-qualification recognition decision, English evidence, CV, motivation statement, health declaration, financial-capacity statement and admission-fee proof. Some academic recognition documents may be submitted later in the procedure.

faq.question: Is English-language evidence required?
faq.answer: Yes, unless the applicant can show four years of English-language learning in secondary school. The call also accepts TOEFL, IELTS or Certificate in Advanced English where previous education was not in English.

faq.question: When does teaching normally begin?
faq.answer: The programme curriculum states that its academic year runs from the beginning of October to the beginning of July. The 2026/27 admission call gives the application deadline but does not publish a cohort-specific first teaching date; the programme is therefore indexed to the October intake period rather than a fixed start-day claim.

faq.question: What clinical training is documented?
faq.answer: The curriculum places clinical rotations in the sixth year and specifies 12 weeks of student practice across Internal Medicine, Surgery, Gynaecology and Paediatrics, with three weeks in each. It does not promise a particular site for a future cohort.

faq.question: Is the school listed internationally?
faq.answer: The school is listed in the World Directory of Medical Schools as currently operational. The listing states that students and graduates may apply for ECFMG Certification for graduation years 1997-current, provided all other ECFMG requirements are met.

faq.question: Can the degree be used to practise medicine abroad?
faq.answer: Professional registration is country-specific. The degree has a WDOMS listing and an ECFMG application-eligibility note, but neither replaces the licensing, examination, language and registration requirements of the country where a graduate plans to practise.

ctas.label: Build my cost and funding plan

fee.notes: The official 2026/27 first call publishes annual tuition of 18,000 BAM and a separate 140 BAM admission fee. The six-year total of 108,000 BAM is calculated from the published annual tuition, not quoted as a lump sum. Tuition is due within one week of the formal electronic acceptance letter and the call states it is non-refundable.

eligibleAudiences: Bosnia and Herzegovina citizens and foreign citizens with completed secondary education or equivalent
Applicants able to document English proficiency through four years of English in secondary school or an accepted TOEFL, IELTS or CAE certificate
restrictions: Selection prioritises the four-year secondary-school average and Biology, Chemistry and Physics grades
Foreign-educated applicants need a Decision on Recognition of Foreign Educational Qualifications; the call allows it later in the procedure
Students on the English programme cannot switch to the Croatian-language Medicine programme and cannot be exempted from tuition
audienceEligibility.notes: The 2026/27 call plans 30 full-time places and closes on 30 September 2026 or once the places are filled.

admissionsContent.overview: Applicants submit the completed application and supporting records by email, post and in person, then provide original documentation at the Student Administration Office. The school confirms receipt by email and the applicant reconfirms that message. Selection prioritises the four-year school average and Biology, Chemistry and Physics grades.

eligibility.intro: Applicants need completed secondary education or an equivalent qualification, documented English ability and the stated health declaration. Foreign qualifications require formal recognition during the admission process.
items: Four-year academic record, including Biology, Chemistry and Physics grades
Proof of four years of English in secondary school, or TOEFL, IELTS or CAE where prior education was not in English
Statement on health and psychophysical ability for medical studies
Decision on Recognition of Foreign Educational Qualifications for prior education completed abroad

applicationSteps: Complete the School of Medicine application form
Prepare academic records, identity documents, English evidence and supporting statements
Pay the 140 BAM admission fee and retain the payment proof
Send the complete application by email, post and in person by the published deadline
Reconfirm the School's email receipt confirmation
Bring original documents to the Student Administration Office
Pay annual tuition within one week of the formal electronic acceptance letter

academic: Secondary-school diploma and two certified copies
Official Croatian translation of the diploma where required
Decision on Recognition of Foreign Educational Qualifications for overseas education
Certificate showing four years of English study or TOEFL, IELTS or CAE

admissionsContent.deadlinesNote: For the 2026/27 first call, applications are due by 30 September 2026 or until all 30 planned places are filled. The programme's curriculum places teaching in an academic year running from the beginning of October to the beginning of July.
visaConsiderations: The official admission call does not publish a student-visa process. International applicants need to plan immigration requirements separately after receiving their admission documentation.

intakeMonths: October intake period; the 2026/27 call gives a 30 September application deadline but no cohort-specific first class date
programmes.feeNotes: Official 2026/27 annual tuition is 18,000 BAM. A separate 140 BAM admission fee applies. Tuition is payable within one week of the formal electronic acceptance letter and is stated as non-refundable; accommodation, living costs, insurance, travel and immigration costs are not included in this programme fee.
